41: The king's authorization helps him even to exempt him if he erred — like the authorization of the Reish Galusa below in siman 25 se'if 2, and so wrote the Rivash; and the Bach wrote that from the words of the Tur it implies that even for one who is gamir and savir the authorization does not help, and not like the Rivash; also not like what is found in the writings of the Maharshal, that for a mumcheh la'rabim the king's authorization helps to exempt him if he erred — for it is not so, but rather it appears clear that he is not exempt, and so wrote the Rambam in his Commentary on the Mishnah (perek Zeh Borer), in this language: "if a king appointed them, etc., if they were mumchim their ruling is a [valid] ruling and accepted, since they did not err, etc.," which shows that where they erred they pay even though they are mumchim — end quote. But his (the Bach's) words are not compelling, for the Tur is not speaking of one who is gamir and savir regarding payment; and likewise the Rambam there is not speaking at all of payment, but rather his intent is to say that if they erred in the din it is reversed, and so it implies there explicitly to one who examines it there. And even though the Tur does not hold this way, nonetheless the reasoning of the Rivash is correct in this, since the authorization of the Reish Galusa, who was appointed by the king, helps in this, all the more so a king or minister himself, for "the law of the kingdom is law" (dina d'malchusa dina), for it is among the statutes of the king and the ministers to appoint judges and dayanim in the land, and if so, it is no worse than the Reish Galusa who comes by his (the king's) authority — analyze this. And see the responsum of the Rama, siman 123.
